solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Relax feeding mate's rodent

indicators.note: to feed something is to put food into it, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: rhyming slang: china plate = mate
to chill is to relax

explanation.surface: Someone is told to unwind while feeding a friend's pet rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: CHINA for mate comes from Cockney rhyming slang, china plate = mate; the 's stands for 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinchilla is a small South American rodent prized for its soft fur.

clue.text: Encourage that man painting edges in emulsion

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

blocks.note: pronoun for a man
painting is a form of art
first and last letters of emulsion

explanation.surface: A decorator is cheered on while he paints the borders of a wall in emulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearten someone is to give them heart, a synonym for encouraging them.

clue.text: Former national leader recalled Number 10 home

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters run back the other way

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for number
Roman numeral for ten
at home means in

explanation.surface: An ex-leader remembers his old residence at Number 10 Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: Number 10 suggests a British Prime Minister, but the leader here is American: NO + X + IN read backwards gives NIXON.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Nixon was President of the United States, a former head of that nation.

clue.text: Attila perhaps with time to seek out recruit

blocks.note: Attila was the head Hun, the leader of the Huns
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Attila the Hun, given time, sets out to find new followers.
explanation.walkthrough: Attila is read as the head Hun: chief of the Huns.
explanation.definitionFit: Headhunting is approaching people to recruit them, typically talent poached from another firm.

clue.text: Very quickly take to appreciative people

blocks.note: to take to something is to like it
people who applaud are the clappers

explanation.surface: Someone warms rapidly to an audience that applauds them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like the clappers' is British informal for very fast, the clappers being the tongues of a bell swung hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom describes moving at great speed, as fast as a bell's clapper flies.

clue.text: All there, soldiers all over fields

indicators.note: over can mean turned over, so the whole string is flipped end to end

blocks.note: to be all there is to be of sound mind
Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: Troops are spread everywhere across the open fields.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a field of activity, a sphere or area where something takes place.

clue.text: Have difficulty breathing and quietly drop back

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read from the end to the start

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
to sag is to drop or droop

explanation.surface: An exhausted person struggles for air and silently slumps backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To gasp is to struggle for breath, taking short, sharp intakes of air.

clue.text: Declining being sent to prison

blocks.note: first meaning: falling, sinking
second meaning: slang for receiving a jail sentence

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a criminal who is 'going down' is about to be jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both decreasing in level and, colloquially, being given a custodial sentence.

clue.text: Bone monster numbly chews

indicators.note: what is chewed is held within the mouth, so the words take the answer inside them

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A beast gnaws on a bone without feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in the middle of monSTER NUMbly.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the breastbone, the flat bone at the front of the chest.

clue.text: Knight overcome by greatest of islanders

indicators.note: something overcome is covered over, so one piece is swallowed by another

blocks.note: max is short for maximum, the greatest
N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A knight is defeated by the best of the island people.
explanation.walkthrough: The Manx are the people of the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manx, as a plural noun, are the natives of the Isle of Man.

clue.text: Child learnt to move with bike

indicators.note: the letters are made to move around into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A youngster has just learnt to get going on a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: An ankle-biter is informal slang for a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: The jokey slang term pictures a toddler at ankle height, so it means a young child.

clue.text: Bad smell adolescent half-heartedly masked in school

indicators.note: half the heart is lost, so one of the two middle letters goes
a masked thing is covered, so it sits hidden inside another piece

blocks.note: abbreviation for school
a teenager

explanation.surface: A teenager unenthusiastically hides a foul odour at school.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-heartedly removes only one of the two middle letters of the four-letter word, not the whole centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a strong, offensive odour.

clue.text: Sound from plucking gnat wing off

indicators.note: off means wrong or not right, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A noise comes from pulling the wing off a gnat.
explanation.definitionFit: Twanging is the resonant noise of a plucked string, as on a guitar.

clue.text: On hospital ward, family surrounding new arrival

indicators.note: to surround something is to enclose it on all sides

blocks.note: ear, nose and throat department
a race is a family line or lineage
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: In a hospital ward, relatives gather round a newborn baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New arrival' suggests a baby, but new is just N and arrival alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrance is a coming in, the act of arriving somewhere.

clue.text: Understand nice ogre's misrepresented

indicators.note: something misrepresented is shown in a false form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the 's supplying an S

explanation.surface: Someone grasps that a kindly ogre has been unfairly portrayed.
explanation.definitionFit: To recognise something can mean to acknowledge or understand it.

clue.text: I'm surprised by mess after emptying units

indicators.note: to empty a word is to take out its insides, leaving only its outermost letters

blocks.note: an exclamation of surprise
first and last letters of mess

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked by the clutter left after clearing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohms are the SI units of electrical resistance.

clue.text: Cold in cooking vessel, evenly heat steak meat

indicators.note: evenly means taking the even-numbered letters: second, fourth and so on

blocks.note: a pan is a cooking vessel
C for cold, as on taps
second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A cook puts something cold in a pan, then heats the steak evenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold in cooking vessel' looks like C inside PAN, but here 'in' just joins: the pieces simply follow on.
explanation.definitionFit: Pancetta is Italian cured pork belly, a type of meat similar to bacon.

clue.text: Spot pronounced design details

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken out, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a speck is a small spot

explanation.surface: Someone notices clearly marked details in a design plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced' looks like an adjective meaning marked, but it signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Spec is short for specification, the detailed description of a design.

clue.text: Fish cut up on bar

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upward

blocks.note: to lop is to cut
to bar a door is to lock it

explanation.surface: A fish is chopped up on a counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollock is a North Atlantic food fish of the cod family.

clue.text: Not so many gaining queen's slender condition

indicators.note: to gain something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: less means fewer, not so many
Queen Anne, British monarch 1702-14

explanation.surface: A queen's thinness is put down to her eating fewer portions.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after queen stands for 'is', linking wordplay to definition rather than adding a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Leanness is the state of being thin, with little fat.

clue.text: Japanese military leader pierced by tip of traditional weapon

indicators.note: a tip is the very front end, so just the opening letter is used
pierced means stuck through, so something is pushed inside

blocks.note: the shogun was Japan's hereditary military ruler
opening letter of traditional

explanation.surface: A Japanese warlord is run through by the point of a traditional weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traditional weapon' reads as a phrase, but only weapon defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun is a smooth-bore firearm that fires many small pellets.

clue.text: Protect top of leg in cast

indicators.note: the top of a down entry's word is its first letter
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: to shy a stone is to throw or cast it
first letter of leg

explanation.surface: A plaster cast guards the upper part of an injured leg.
explanation.walkthrough: Cast suggests a plaster cast; here it is the past tense meaning threw.
explanation.definitionFit: To shield someone is to guard them from harm, a synonym of protect.

clue.text: Loud convicts in important vessel

blocks.note: f (forte) is the musical marking for loud
old lags are British slang for long-term prisoners
in fashion means hip

explanation.surface: Noisy prisoners are held aboard a major ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal but is a word meaning fashionable; lags is British slang for convicts.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagship is the leading ship of a fleet, carrying the admiral's flag.

clue.text: One imprisons degenerate gang briefly in revolution

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped
revolving turns the whole sequence round to run the other way

blocks.note: to rot is to decay or degenerate
a pack is a gang

explanation.surface: Someone locks up a corrupt gang for a short while during a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: PACK loses its last letter, joins ROT, and the whole is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A captor is a person who takes and holds someone prisoner.

clue.text: Arrogant pair, couple from south

indicators.note: in a down entry, starting from the south means reading upward

blocks.note: abbreviation for pair
a duo is a couple

explanation.surface: A conceited pair of southerners are described.
explanation.definitionFit: Proud can mean haughty, having too high an opinion of oneself.

clue.text: Try to remain determined taking runs in desolate area

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: have a go, a try
to bide is to stay or remain
set on something means determined
R for runs in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stay resolute after being run out into wild country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi Desert is a vast arid region in Mongolia and northern China.

clue.text: Gallons shifted in distasteful drunken revelry

indicators.note: the gallons abbreviation is moved to a new place within the word, rearranging it

blocks.note: gory means bloody and distasteful

explanation.surface: Gallons of drink are moved around in some unpleasant drunken partying.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one letter moves: the G at the front of GORY slides to third place.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a wild party marked by excessive drinking and indulgence.

clue.text: Baked peeled eastern fruit

indicators.note: peeling removes the outer skin, leaving only the inner letters

blocks.note: baked without its first and last letters
E for eastern

explanation.surface: A baked, skinned fruit from the East is served.
explanation.definitionFit: The akee (ackee) is a tropical fruit, eaten with saltfish in Jamaica.

clue.text: Scrapping inspector's vehicle with slight damage

blocks.note: DI, detective inspector, with the possessive S
a car is a vehicle
a ding is a small dent

explanation.surface: A detective's car is being scrapped after a minor bump.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarding means throwing away, getting rid of something as useless.
